analysis.title: Commodity Comment: Long Game
key_insights: RBC says the nine-month Iran conflict risks running longer and being more disruptive than some expect. Neither the current stalemate nor an escalation-to-exit scenario gives a beneficial backdrop for elevated exports or production over the next 6-9 months.

Market observers are focused on exports moving through Hormuz and assume most of the disruption is past. Security experts in Washington and the region are alarmed by Iran's willingness to escalate. RBC notes that White House 'over soon' messaging has contributed to the short-duration view.

Post-WWII interstate conflicts averaged 2.1 years, so short wars are an anomaly. RBC cites Washington conversations saying Iran shows no sign of dropping its maximalist demands for full enforcement of the June MoU despite the blockade's economic cost.

Proponents of the blockade strategy concede it needs a significant amount of time, with estimates from 8-9 additional months to as long as 2 years. Tehran is expected to keep escalating strikes on Hormuz tankers and US military assets, with Kuwait and Bahrain bearing the brunt of recent Iranian fire.

RBC questions whether elevated exports could be maintained in a hasty US withdrawal, especially if US military assets aiding transits are removed and there is no maritime management agreement among key regional players.

Middle East crude loadings have averaged about 4.9 mb/d below pre-war (Jan-Feb) levels over the last four weeks. Loadings outside Hormuz are about 1 mb/d above pre-war because of re-routing (e.g. via East-West). Mideast Gulf loadings inside Hormuz are down about 5.9 mb/d.

Initial loadings this week are lower both inside and outside Hormuz. 7-day moving average commodity vessel transits in the Strait are down over 50% over the last 30 days. RBC says this reinforces its fundamental view despite the sentiment shift in oil markets.

Natural gas prices rose midweek as colder forecasts through late November raised HDD forecasts. The cold snap is expected to be short-lived, and medium-term forecasts through December still show HDDs 4% below seasonal norms, consistent with a mild El Niño winter.

Near-record LNG feedgas demand has held through November and limits the market's ability to absorb weather-driven consumption increases. The inventory surplus is intact, but sustained exports and intermittent cold could erode it. RBC calls the broader outlook bearish for rescomm, with tightening balances giving intermittent upside support.

Gold has fallen into the low $3,700s on hawkish Fed commentary and yields above 5%. RBC points to its low scenario of $3,661/oz in 2027 as where gold should find fundamental support, and says its 2027-2028 conviction is unchanged.

Governor Waller said yesterday that inflation is still going in the wrong direction and urged a more aggressive rate hike. RBC argues much of the bad news is priced in, and that central bank appetite, investor allocations, equity volatility and uncertainty remain supports. It calls inflation a fickle driver that can move gold either way.
US installed power capacity rose 12% y/y in the first three quarters of 2026. Onshore wind added 6.4 GW through September, up 84% y/y, largely due to a 3.5 GW project in New Mexico in May.

Renewable capacity growth slowed to 8% in 2026 from 19% in 2025 and 62% in 2024. New solar capacity is down 10% y/y through September after an 11% y/y decline in 2025. RBC cites trade, tariff, policy and finance headwinds, which could increase if data center demand for clean energy declines.

CFTC managed money data as of 10-Nov-26 show gold net long at 27.8% of futures open interest (26.0% a week earlier) and natural gas at -13.7% (-13.4%). Crude on Nymex is 1.3% net long and ICE crude is -1.8%.
Swap dealers are net short gold at -51.1% of futures open interest (-49.1% a week earlier) and Nymex crude at -24.5%. Silver is -18.3% and ICE crude -12.8%.
RBC's middle-scenario oil forecasts are WTI $86 and Brent $91 for 2026, and WTI $83 and Brent $88 for 2027. Its 2026 balance shows a 3.1 mb/d deficit, with the Q3 2026 deficit at 5.3 mb/d.

RBC's gold middle scenario averages $4,503/oz for 2026 and $4,225/oz for 2027, with the 2027 low scenario at $3,661 and the high at $5,296. Its natural gas middle scenario is $3.29/MMBtu for 2026 and $3.84 for 2027.
The weekly calendar lists the FOMC rate decision on 9-Dec, US CPI on 10-Dec, the US jobs report on 4-Dec, ISM Manufacturing on 1-Dec and US GDP in the week of 23-Nov.

sector_views.rationale: RBC's fundamental view is that Middle East exports and Hormuz transits are receding and the conflict is likely to be prolonged. Its forecasts show supply deficits through 2026.
The broader outlook is bearish for rescomm given the inventory surplus and a mild winter outlook. Near-record LNG feedgas demand may give intermittent upside support.
RBC says structural supports are intact, with central bank and investor demand strong and a floor near its $3,661/oz 2027 low scenario.
New solar capacity is down 10% y/y through September, with trade, tariff, policy and finance headwinds.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Gold is retreating on Fed hawkishness and elevated yields. RBC sees support near its $3,661/oz 2027 low scenario.
RBC calls yields above 5% a hurdle for gold regardless of other drivers.

tension_points.bull_case: Some market observers assume the bulk of the disruption is behind and are focused on exports moving through Hormuz. The White House 'over soon' messaging supports a short-duration view.
tension_points.bear_case: RBC says Iran shows no sign of dropping its maximalist demands and is escalating strikes on tankers and US assets. Loadings inside Hormuz are down about 5.9 mb/d and transits are down over 50% in 30 days, so the stalemate and a US exit both look unfavorable for exports and production over 6-9 months.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained recovery in Mideast Gulf crude loadings and Hormuz transits, which RBC says the trajectory does not currently show.

tension_points.bull_case: Central bank appetite and investor allocations remain strong, equity volatility persists, and RBC says a lot of the bad news is priced in. Inflation can move gold either way.
tension_points.bear_case: Hawkish Fed commentary, including Governor Waller urging a more aggressive hike, and yields above 5% are a hurdle for gold.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A move below RBC's low scenario of $3,661/oz in 2027, the level where it expects fundamental support.

tension_points.bull_case: Near-record LNG feedgas demand has held through November, and sustained exports plus intermittent cold could erode the inventory surplus, giving intermittent upside support.
tension_points.bear_case: The inventory surplus is intact, HDDs are forecast 4% below seasonal norms through December, and the broader outlook is bearish for rescomm.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Signs of sustained inventory erosion in the coming weeks, especially if colder weather forecasts materialize alongside elevated LNG demand.
